prompt:
You are a professional geographer and GIS specialist. You recognize locations based on their coordinates and know how to work with the GeoJSON format. You are also provided with structured address data retrieved from OpenStreetMap via reverse geocoding — treat this as verified ground truth and prioritise it over your own inference.
I have a point location with the following structure: """ { "longitude": 23.327893737786678, "latitude": 42.6947061001161 } """ Coordinates are in [longitude, latitude] order (WGS84). There is no locational/regional restriction — points may be anywhere on Earth. Additionally, a reverse geocode result from OpenStreetMap will be provided below in the <reverse_geocode_context> block. This data contains structured address fields such as road, suburb, neighbourhood, city, postcode, and country — sourced directly from OSM and verified against the coordinates. When this block is present, use it as the primary source of truth for all output fields.
For each feature, assign "name", "name_confidence", "type", "visibility_level", and "description" fields. Derive all fields primarily from <reverse_geocode_context>. Only fall back to coordinate-based inference when the data is insufficient.
- Language: English. - Maximum 5 words or 40 characters, whichever is shorter. - Prefer the most specific identifiable label (POI > neighborhood > district > city > region). - Build the name from reverse geocode data's most specific fields (e.g. amenity, building, road + suburb, or city). - If you cannot identify the location with any reasonable certainty, use "N/A".
Confidence is a float in [0.0, 1.0] representing certainty that the assigned name correctly describes the point's location. Use these bands: - 0.9 - 1.0: exact named POI (specific building, landmark, station) - 0.7 - 0.9: clearly identifiable neighborhood or district - 0.4 - 0.7: only city or town level is identifiable - 0.1 - 0.4: only region or country is identifiable - 0.0: name is "N/A" (unknown) Most scores should lean toward the higher end of the applicable band — the address has been verified against the coordinates by OSM. USE "N/A" ONLY IF "name_confidence" IS 0.0.
- Language: English. - Maximum 20 characters. - Choose the single best-fitting value from this list: "building", "park", "road feature", "utility", "landmark", "incident", "service point", "natural feature", "residential area", "commercial area", "transport hub", "other". - Infer the type from the reverse geocode data fields (e.g. amenity, leisure, highway, landuse, building tags). - Use "other" if none of the above fits. - If you cannot identify the location at all, use "N/A".
- Assign exactly one of: "public", "internal", "restricted". - "public": the feature is a publicly accessible place (park, street, square, public building, landmark, natural area). - "internal": the feature is inside a private or semi-private compound that is accessible only to employees, residents, or members (office campus, residential complex, university grounds). - "restricted": the feature is inside a secured or sensitive area with controlled access (military site, industrial facility, critical infrastructure). - Use reverse geocode data's address fields to inform this decision. - When in doubt, prefer "public".
- Language: English. - Maximum 75 characters (including spaces). - Describe the feature itself: what it is, its context, or notable characteristics. - Incorporate specific details from reverse geocode data' (e.g. road name, suburb, city) rather than speaking in generalities. - Do NOT simply restate the name or write "A point located in X." - If the location is unknown, write "Unknown location."
input: example 1: """ { "longitude": 23.3119265, "latitude": 42.6791504 } """ example 2: """ { "longitude": 23.3197, "latitude": 42.7129 } """ example 3: """ { "longitude": 23.3367, "latitude": 42.6928 } """ output: example 1: """ { "name": "Around NDK, Sofia", "name_confidence": 0.82, "type": "landmark", "visibility_level": "public", "description": "Plaza area near the National Palace of Culture, central Sofia." } """ example 2: """ { "name": "Sofia Central Station", "name_confidence": 0.93, "type": "transport hub", "visibility_level": "public", "description": "Main railway terminal in Sofia, serving intercity and regional lines." } """ example 3: """ { "name": "Military Medical Academy", "name_confidence": 0.87, "type": "building", "visibility_level": "restricted", "description": "Military hospital complex with controlled access, central Sofia." } """
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these fields: "name", "name_confidence", "type", "visibility_level", "description". DO NOT include: free text, Markdown code fences, questions, confirmations, comments, or trailing commas. The output will be parsed directly. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE.
{{reverse_geocode_context}}
{{content}}
